sourceText:
Spicy Green Tomato Vinaigrette
By: Natalie (Perrys...
Published: Thursday, November 4, 2010 - 4:35pm

Ingredients




high heat-safe oil for drizzling (coconut, grapeseed, etc.)
1/2 pound green tomatoes
1 large red tomato
1 jalapeno pepper
1/4 cup coarsely chopped onion
1 clove garlic, peeled and quartered
2 tablespoons white or white wine vinegar
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 pinch big of salt and black pepper
1 1/2 teaspoons honey or agave nectar
1/4 cup coarsely chopped fresh cilantro

Preparation

1 Preheat BBQ grill or stove-top grill pan to medium heat. 2 Wash tomatoes and jalapeno, pat dry, then put them in a medium bowl. Drizzle with oil and toss to coat. 3 Place vegetables on preheated grill. Grill for 10-15 minutes, turning 2 or 3 times, until tomatoes have softened, and both the tomatoes and jalapenos have black grill marks. Remove from grill and set aside until cool enough to handle. 4 Quarter tomatoes, removing leaves and place in a blender or food processor. Remove jalapeno stem, seeds, and white-colored veins. (Unless you want this really spicy, then leave a bit in there.) Place jalapeno along with the remaining ingredients into the blender with the tomatoes. Process until smooth. Taste to check seasonings. If it's too acidic, add a little more sweetener and maybe a pinch of salt. 5 Transfer to a sealed container (I like glass mason jars) and chill. Keeps in the fridge for about 2 weeks.

About


1. To make salsa instead, omit the vinegar and oil and add the juice from one lime. Process until slightly chunky.
2. If you aren't able to grill, you could roast the vegetables instead.  Put them all on a rimmed baking sheet and broil, turning occasionally, until they get soft and black spots appear. I'm not sure how long it will take because I didn't do it this way, but I would estimate about 10-15 minutes.
